channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: NFL would cancel Paris game if unsafe due to protests, Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers says
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers said Friday the NFL would have cancelled its first regular-season game in Paris if the situation were unsafe due to recent mass protests. The Steelers are scheduled to face the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France in the Paris suburb of ​Saint-Denis on Sunday.

item.title: Netanyahu orders West Bank operation
item.description: Israel has imposed widespread closures across the occupied West Bank and displaced residents following attacks by Palestinian gunmen that killed two Israeli soldiers. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited the site of the attack near Hebron and instructed security forces to immediately cordon off the city. Morgan Ayre reports.

item.title: Typhoon Champi batters Taiwan
item.description: Typhoon Champi is heading towards China and Japan. Yesterday, it battered Taiwan with heavy rain and winds reaching up to 180 kilometres per hour. Across the island, 56,000 households are without power. Nicolas Chamontin and Ophelie Jacobson report.

item.title: French students vow to keep protesting
item.description: Amid growing concerns over violence, people across France, young and old alike, are weighing up whether taking part in demonstrations is worth the risk. France 24’s Ophelie Jackson reports.

item.title: France: March against National Rally in Orleans
item.description: Against this backdrop of heightened tensions, France’s far-right National Rally is holding its annual congress in Orléans, south of Paris, where it is expected to officially launch Marine Le Pen’s presidential campaign and re-elect Jordan Bardella as party leader. Thousands of supporters are expected to attend, while a major counter-demonstration has been organised against racism, fascism and imperialism. Local authorities are preparing for possible clashes between the two groups. Antonia Kerrigan reports the latest.

item.title: Paris: Last-minute change to the protest route
item.description: The Paris police prefecture changed the route of the authorised trade union march at the last minute ahead of the 24 October mobilisation. The new route runs between Place d’Italie and Porte de Vincennes. But this morning, many protesters turned up at Place de la Bastille, the march’s original starting point, before the route was changed, leaving them confused and unsure where to go. France 24 journalist Elitsa Gadeva brings us the latest from the scene.

item.title: Is your Medicare Advantage plan ending next year? Here's what to know
item.description: Medicare open enrollment runs through Dec. 7, and for as many as 5 million seniors, it will be important to log on and pick a new plan.

item.title: U.S. birth rate drops to record low, but older women are having more babies
item.description: The U.S. birth rate fell to its lowest level ever recorded, according to a report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The drop would have been greater, but women over age 30 are having more children.

item.title: Ukraine says Starlink and Starshield connection 'stable' again
item.description: Ukraine has regained a "stable" connection to the Starlink and Starshield satellite communications systems, Kyiv's defence minister said on Saturday. Recent disruptions to the connection led to tensions with Washington over the SpaceX-made network crucial to the Ukrainian army's operations.

item.title: Bahamas police investigate after British woman dies trying to rescue sons
item.description: Police are investigating after a British woman died while trying to rescue her two sons off the Bahamas coast.

item.title: This decade has been missing its big-impact midterm
item.description: Every other decade over the past hundred years has produced at least one midterm that made a big difference in Congress and in national politics more broadly.

item.title: Protests against cost of living expected in Italy under heavy security
item.description: Italy is preparing for another day of protests on Saturday against budget cuts and the high cost of living in eight cities, including Rome and Milan. Following last weekend’s unrest, authorities announced heavy security measures, including the use of drones and helicopters to monitor the marches.

item.title: Drinking water supplies dwindle in Yemeni city besieged by Houthi rebels
item.description: Taiz, a city in southwestern Yemen, faces a severe water crisis as Houthi rebels backed by Iran tighten their encirclement. The city has struggled with water issues for over a decade, but the situation has worsened in recent weeks.

item.title: Former Goldman Sachs chief leaves Britain amid tax hike fears
item.description: A former Goldman Sachs chief who sits on the board of Revolut, Europe's most valuable private technology company, has become the latest prominent financier to leave the country amid concerns about Britain’s rising tax burden.

item.title: French police deploy in large numbers, major Paris museums close ahead of new protests
item.description: France will deploy about 70,000 police nationwide and some of Paris' major museums will close Saturday as the country braces for a fresh wave of protests after looting and unrest erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations a week ago. Another massive turnout is expected after more than a half million took to the streets last week.

item.title: German teen arrested on suspicion of murder in connection with US girl's death
item.description: The 18-year-old is accused of manipulating an Indiana teen over a social platform, according to prosecutors in Germany.

item.title: Live: France braces for fresh wave of protests amid high tensions
item.description: A coalition of the “Yellow Vests” movement, trade unions and students will march across France on Saturday with demands over studying conditions and purchasing power. Some 70,000 police are expected to be deployed as authorities fear looting and vandalism similar to last Saturday's unrest. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: Suspect arrested after fire at Hitler's 'Eagle's Nest' retreat
item.description: Police have detained a suspect after a fire erupted at a historic Nazi mountain retreat known as "Eagle's Nest" in Germany.

item.title: UK pledges £600m to defend against AI health and security threats
item.description: The UK has pledged to spend £600m to defend the public against threats to health and security from artificial intelligence.

item.title: Britt McHenry resigns from State Department after basketball game altercation
item.description: The former ESPN reporter was appointed as a press adviser last month.

item.title: Hero dad who took down school shooter speaks out: 'I was supposed to be there'
item.description: Kaylub Giamanco said he was driving home on Oct. 15 when he saw a person in all black, armed with a gun, jump over the fence at the elementary school.

item.title: WATCH: 2 rescued from sinking boat off Florida coast
item.description: Dramatic video shows the rescue of two people stranded in the ocean after their boat sunk off the coast of Fort Myers, Florida. Both boaters are doing OK.

item.title: 'I heard children pleading': Father reveals how he stopped Oregon school shooter
item.description: A father has described how he shot the gunman who killed four people at his daughter's school in Oregon and the guilt he feels about the "ones that I didn't save".

item.title: Severe flooding hits Four Corners region, more expected through the weekend
item.description: Intense rainfall slammed the Four Corners region late this week. As rivers flooded, towns declared evacuations and emergencies and made rescues.

item.title: Jane Doe in Cornell lawsuit to remain anonymous as judge warns against threats
item.description: The judge said "the notoriety of the allegations and widespread reports of certain malicious actors' behavior" warranted anonymity.

item.title: In tight race for Ga. gov, Keisha Lance Bottoms has been outspent but still confident
item.description: The GOP candidate Rick Jackson is a healthcare executive and billionaire.

item.title: Why Burnham has had to defend his Gogglebox double act
item.description: They looked like a modern-day Morecambe and Wise. But at least they weren't sharing a bed like the famous comic duo.

item.title: WATCH: Nat Geo’s 'Moment on the Earth' showcases stunning snorkel cam footage
item.description: National Geographic’s Wonderlab Snorkel Cam, created by Explorer Anand Varma, captures striking 360-degree views of ocean creatures, including a barnacle-covered mussel and a sea urchin.

item.title: Russia steps up election influence efforts in final stretch of midterms
item.description: Researchers who track online influence operations say Kremlin-backed groups are renewing tactics they've used to sow distrust and discord in previous elections in the U.S. and around the world.

item.title: Trump doubles down on Amy Acton criticism as Ramaswamy ad controversy swirls
item.description: "It's a mother speaking badly against Amy Acton," Trump said.

item.title: Trump says US may launch ‘another little Epic Fury’ attack on Iran
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Friday said his country may launch “another little Epic Fury” on Iran, referring to the joint Israeli-American military operation that sparked the war with Iran at the end of February.

item.title: Building collapse in Nairobi search for survivors under way
item.description: In tonight's programme, scramble to get through rubble to trapped survivors after a more than 10 storeys building being built in Nairobi goes down. Also, Kenya says that there's been a second Ebola death. Earlier this week it had logged 9 cases so far, all traced back to its first Ebola patient who died earlier this month. And in finally the 11th edition of the iconic contemporary art festival Also known as Africa taking place in Paris, we speak to Cape Verde's artist Amadeo Carvalho.

item.title: The Pentagon's guidelines for "responsible AI" aren't always followed, report shows
item.description: The Pentagon is building weapons and projects with AI capabilities that officials say don't always closely adhere to the agency's own guidelines for AI, according to a congressional watchdog report published in October.

item.title: Why Trump told Burnham the UK is going to be 'very rich'
item.description: Donald Trump has said he told Andy Burnham the UK is set to become "a very rich country" after the prime minister decided to allow drilling in the North Sea.

item.title: First lady Melania Trump says she brokered 'temporary' ceasefire in Ukrainian town
item.description: It's unclear exactly how long the ceasefire is set to last.

item.title: After French Riots, Curfews & Calm .. is a new Storm Brewing ? Plus Ukraine & Israel
item.description: It's been a week that’s seen mass protests hijacked by violent rioters across France. The looting of shops, trashing of public buildings, the burning of Lyon’s Tourist Information and the iconic Limoges City Hall. After the riots, came the curfews, and the contemplation, who did what and why weren’t they stopped. Seditious groups, ultra left anarchists and opportunist criminals said President Macron, with a qualified mea culpa: failures in anticipation and authorities dropped the ball in intelligence gathering. Macron is out of breath, exhausted and disorientated claimed the Presidential Frontrunner Marine Le Pen, the far right leader now polling in an even stronger position for the Presidency. Foreign leaders had a free for all too, President Trump wading in and Israel’s prime minister settled old scores ahead of elections there. But France wasn’t isolated in its protests and unrest, Milan was a mirror image, with demonstrations in Spain, Portugal, Belgium too, An Autumn of Discontent

item.title: Ohio could decide control of the Senate. Its rural voters might decide the winner
item.description: Ohio has been a reliably red state for several elections but it's competitive this year. If Democrats want to prevail, they'll have to win people who have backed Republicans, like rural voters.

item.title: Netanyahu weighs West Bank operation ahead of elections: ‘Politically, it will not help anybody’
item.description: As Israel approaches a consequential parliamentary election amid renewed violence in the occupied West Bank, Yedioth Ahronoth Senior Journalist Ben-Dror Yemini offers a critical assessment of Benjamin Netanyahu's political prospects, the limits of military escalation and the shifting relationship between national security and electoral legitimacy. Since October 7, 2023 "Netanyahu is not popular anymore," Yemini argues, identifying the Hamas-led attacks as a decisive turning point in the Israeli prime minister's public standing.

item.title: A D.C. park was made 'for the pleasure of the people.' Trump's plan would change that
item.description: Trump's most recent rendering of East Potomac Park overtakes the D.C. peninsula with a sprawling golf course, without the grassy areas and road beloved by locals. That's prompted grassroots pushback.

item.title: How Israeli settlers wearing keffiyehs are attacking West Bank olive groves
item.description: The olive harvest officially began in the West Bank on October 15, 2026, and it has coincided with an uptick in violence towards Palestinians carried out by both Israeli settlers and soldiers. Meanwhile, the settlers and soldiers have been using social media to promote an aesthetic, Instagram-friendly and nationalistic view of these harvests.

item.title: Israel: Could Arab parties play kingmaker in the next Knesset ?
item.description: As Israelis head to the polls for the first legislative election since Hamas's October 7 attacks, neither Prime Minister Benjamin #Netanyahu's Likud party nor former army chief of staff Gadi #Eisenkot's Yashar party are likely to win a majority of seats in the #Knesset. Turns out, #Israel's Arab parties could have a say in the election's outcome.

item.title: Gaza : digging up the bodies from under the rubble
item.description: One year after the ceasefire in Gaza, efforts to recover the bodies buried beneath the rubble are continuing. Civil Defense officials say 1,000 bodies have been recovered so far, but the task remains immense: between 8,000 and 10,000 more are still believed to be buried under the debris, including 3,000 in areas controlled by the Israeli army.

item.title: WATCH: Knicks coaches waiting on rings, staffers hit by phishing email: Report
item.description: New York Knicks assistant coaches did not receive their championship rings during Tuesday's title ceremony, according to a report.

item.title: Vincent Kompany taken to hospital after collapsing at Bayern Munich training
item.description: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany has been taken to hospital after collapsing at the club's training ground.

item.title: 2 ex-FBI officials charged with making false statements about Hunter Biden's laptop
item.description: Two former FBI intelligence officials who specialized in foreign election interference have been charged with making false statements about their roles in investigating the origins of Hunter Biden’s laptop in the run-up to the 2020 presidential election

item.title: West Bank: Extensive military operation 'on the way', Netanyahu says
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday warned of an imminent large-scale military operation in the West Bank and vowed to displace some residents of Hebron after Palestinian gunmen killed two soldiers in an attack.

item.title: Yes, Israeli settlers are ripping up West Bank olive trees – but this video is fake
item.description: Israeli settlers and soldiers have made a habit of destroying olive trees grown by Palestinian farmers in the West Bank and, in recent days, a video showing some trees being ripped up has circulated online. Just one problem: this particular video was generated by artificial intelligence.

item.title: Ex-FBI employees charged with lying to Congress over Hunter Biden inquiries
item.description: Republicans have long accused the FBI of mishandling the laptop and the investigations into the younger Biden.

item.title: AKAA art and design fair brings African artists to Paris
item.description: Every year the art and design fair AKAA, or "Also Known as Africa", brings dozens of African and Afro-descendant artists to the French capital. As the 11th edition gets underway, we welcome Nigerian painter Midegbeyan Ojisua and South African artist Olivié Keck.

item.title: Europe faces threat of organised sabotage, terrorist attacks: Estonian FM Tsahkna
item.description: Estonia's counterintelligence service has recently warned that sabotage operations orchestrated by Russian special services have reached a new and dangerous phase in Europe, with targets no longer being purely symbolic. Talking Europe sits down with the country's foreign minister, Margus Tsahkna, to discuss the security situation in Estonia and the European Union in general.

item.title: EU member states wrangle over all-important budget: Is a deal this year feasible?
item.description: A marathon EU summit on October 15-16 failed to produce a breakthrough on the European Union's next long-term budget. Although EU leaders put on a brave face at the end of the talks by saying that "the way forward is clearer", EU capitals appear deadlocked on what that path is. At stake is the EU's ability to finance its strategic priorities from 2028 to 2034. The main dividing line is between the so-called "frugal countries", who want deep cuts to the proposed budget, and the "friends of cohesion", who say that cuts are not the answer.

item.title: WATCH: Billy Idol surprises students with musical instruments
item.description: The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inductee visited Griffiths Middle School in Downey, California, to surprise students at two local schools with new musical instruments.

item.title: Gas prices unlikely to drop below $4 before midterms, some experts say. Here's why.
item.description: High gas prices continue to weigh on wallets as voters list affordability as a top concern ahead of early November's midterm elections.

item.title: Former Olympic marathon champion suspended after failed drugs test
item.description: Former Olympic and world marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir has been provisionally suspended after testing positive for the banned substance EPO, officials have said.

item.title: Seven dead and 34 injured after shooting at church in Jordan
item.description: Seven people have died and 34 have been injured after gunmen opened fire on a funeral at a church in Jordan.

item.title: WATCH: Woman makes history swimming the entire California coast
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to Catherine Breed, who made history by swimming the nearly 900-mile route in just 111 days.

item.title: WATCH: New Jersey mayor defends charging critic during town hall meeting
item.description: Chaos unfolded during a town hall meeting in Pemberton, New Jersey, after Mayor Matthew Bianchini charged at a critic before being restrained by a former police chief.

item.title: Trump slams LeBron James over apparent national anthem stretches
item.description: President Donald Trump criticized James for appearing to stretch during the national anthem ahead of his 76ers debut.

item.title: Buttigieg endorses independent over Democratic nominee in Montana Senate race
item.description: Pete Buttigieg is endorsing independent Montana U.S. Senate candidate Seth Bodnar.

item.title: Israel orders army to prepare to fully close West Bank after two soldiers killed in shooting
item.description: The Israeli government has ordered its army to prepare for a full closure of the occupied West Bank following a shooting near Hebron which killed two soldiers.

item.title: Pentagon directive bans troops from using nonpublic info to bet in prediction markets
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has issued a new directive telling troops they cannot use “nonpublic information” to make bets on prediction markets

item.title: WATCH: 12-year-old 'Captain William' goes viral after Delta DREAM Flight
item.description: Aspiring pilot William Hobson, 12, is winning hearts online after showing off his impressive in-flight lingo aboard Delta’s DREAM Flight.

item.title: Meghan's father investigated by police over child sex abuse image claims
item.description: The Duchess of Sussex has said she is "deeply distressed" by allegations that her estranged father possessed child sex abuse images.

item.title: Terrorist shooting in Paris suburb marks 'turning point for France', Macron says
item.description: Emmanuel Macron has described the fatal shooting in a Paris suburb as a terrorist and racist attack which "marked a turning point" in the history of France.

item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: WATCH: Inside the North Carolina State Fair
item.description: ABC News' Leslie Lopez reports from Raleigh, where the North Carolina State Fair is underway and has already drawn hundreds of thousands of visitors.

item.title: WATCH: David Muir on how Tampa Bay community came together to repair stadium for Rays
item.description: As the Tampa Bay Rays and their fans prepare for the World Series, David Muir reports on how the community rebuilt the city and repair Tropicana Field after Hurricane Milton.

item.title: WATCH: 7-year-old singer wins hearts on the street, social media
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to Jordan Sunshine, a boy in California who found therapy for his anxiety by performing on the streets of Los Angeles.

item.title: WATCH: American farms honor Dolly Parton with themed corn maze
item.description: Nearly two dozen farms across the country are featuring a Dolly Parton themed corn maze this fall. ABC News' Reena Roy takes us along as she finds her way through one of them in New Jersey.

item.title: WATCH: National Geographic reveals 'Best of the World' destinations
item.description: National Geographic editor-in-chief Nathan Lump talks about must-visit destinations for 2027.
